Driving is a privilege - not a right
Ontario is a road safety leader in Canada and North America.
The Ministry of Transportation has introduced a range of measures to maintain this record and to improve the behaviour of all drivers.
Most collisions are caused by driver error or behaviours such as following too closely, speeding, failure to yield the right of way, improper turns, running red lights and frequently changing lanes.
There are also drivers who intentionally put others at risk through such reckless behaviour.
Statistics show that new drivers of all ages are far more likely than experienced drivers to be involved in serious or fatal collisions.
Provincial campaigns promoting the correct use of seatbelts and child car seats, and informing people about drinking and driving and aggressive driving, are making a difference.
Ontario’s Graduated Licensing System (GLS), which lets new drivers gain skills and experience in low-risk environments, is also helping to develop better, safer drivers.

This handbook gives new drivers the basic information they need about learning to drive in Ontario: the rules of the road, safe driving practices and how to get a licence to drive a car, van or small truck.
The ministry recommends that all drivers would benefit from taking an advanced course in driver training.

New drivers applying for their first car or motorcycle licence enter Ontario’s graduated licensing system.
Graduated licensing lets new drivers get driving experience and skills gradually.
The two-step licensing process takes at least 20 months to complete.
To apply for a licence, you must be at least 16 years old, pass a vision test and pass a test of your knowledge of the rules of the road and traffic signs.

label.v: a licence applicant MUST be at least 16 years old AND pass a vision test AND pass a knowledge test of the rules of the road and traffic signs WHEN the applicant applies for a licence

You must pass two road tests to become fully licensed.

label.v: a novice driver MUST pass two road tests to become fully licensed

text: Passing the first road test lets you move to Level Two (Class G2), and the second one gives you full Class G driving privileges.
To apply for a licence, you must show proof of your legal name and date of birth (showing day, month and year of birth).

text: Seatbelts and child car seats save lives
Seatbelts and child car seats reduce the risk of injury or death in collisions.
Seatbelts help keep you inside and in control of the vehicle during a collision.
People who are thrown from a vehicle have a much lower chance of surviving a collision.
Seatbelts keep your head and body from hitting the inside of the vehicle or another person in the vehicle.
When a vehicle hits a solid object, the people inside keep moving until something stops them.
If you are not wearing your seatbelt, the steering wheel, windshield, dashboard or another person might be what stops you.
This “human collision” often causes serious injury.
Fire or sinking in water is rare in collisions.
If it does happen, seatbelts help keep you conscious, giving you a chance to get out of the vehicle.
In a sudden stop or swerve, no one can hold onto a child who is not in a seatbelt or child car seat.
Infants or children who are not properly restrained can be thrown against the vehicle’s interior, collide with other people or be ejected.

text: By the end of this section, you should know:

text: To give yourself a two-second space, follow these steps:

text: Pick a marker on the road ahead, such as a road sign or telephone pole.

label.v: STEP 1 pick a marker on the road ahead, such as a road sign OR telephone pole

label.v: STEP 2 count 'one thousand and one, one thousand and two' WHEN the rear of the vehicle ahead passes the marker

text: When the front of your vehicle reaches the marker, stop counting.

text: By the end of this section you should know:

Ontario’s roads accommodate many road users, including pedestrians, motorcycles, bicycles, large trucks, buses and farm machinery.

label.v: a driver SHOULD WATCH FOR other road users, the speed at which they travel AND the space they occupy on the road

text: About 100 people are killed and 16,000 are injured by distracted drivers every year in Ontario.
About one in four of those deaths are vulnerable road users such as pedestrians and cyclists.
Research shows that young people 16-25 are more likely to drive distracted than any age group and are the most likely to be killed or injured in a distracted driving collision.
Texting or browsing on your phone takes your eyes off the road and increases your risk of crashing by 10 times.

In fact, a recent study found that drivers who were texting or changing music on their phones traveled 28 metres further (nearly half a hockey rink) before responding to a hazard than drivers who were paying attention.
It can be a matter of life and death for a child who runs out on the street unexpectedly, or a family crossing at a crosswalk.

Vehicles powered by gasoline and diesel give off air pollutants and gases such as oxides of carbon, nitrogen and sulphur, hydrocarbons and soot.
These pollutants affect the quality of the air we breathe, our health, crop yields and even the global climate.
Hydrocarbons and oxides of nitrogen react in sunlight to form ground-level ozone, better known as smog.

label.v: DEFINE ground-level ozone IS a pollutant THAT forms when hydrocarbons AND oxides of nitrogen react in sunlight ALSO CALLED smog

text: Smog is a major health hazard responsible for respiratory ailments and other illnesses.
Oxides of sulphur and nitrogen combine with water vapour to form acid rain, which damages our lakes, forests and crops.
Global warming is the result of too much carbon dioxide and other gases trapping heat in our atmosphere.
Global warming could cause average temperatures to rise, causing droughts, crop failures, lower water levels and more frequent and severe storms.
A car gives off less carbon dioxide than a larger vehicle, such as an airplane, truck, bus or train, does.
However, because so many people own cars and drive them so often, cars are responsible for nearly half the carbon dioxide produced by all forms of transportation.
Vehicles that carry large numbers of passengers, such as buses, produce less carbon dioxide per passenger than cars.
As a driver, you can help to protect the environment from the harmful effects of driving by following these suggestions.
Many of them can also save you money.
For further information visit the Fleetsmart website.

Traffic laws include the traffic signs and lights, pedestrian signals and pavement markings that tell drivers and other road users what they must do in certain situations.
This chapter shows you what many of those signs, lights and markings look like and explains what they mean to drivers.
Signs
Traffic lights
Pedestrian signals
Pavement markings
Traffic signs give you important information about the law, warn you about dangerous conditions and help you find your way.

Statistics show that new drivers of all ages are far more likely than experienced drivers to be involved in serious or fatal collisions.
To help new drivers develop better, safer driving habits, Ontario introduced graduated licensing in 1994 for all drivers applying for their first car or motorcycle licence.
Graduated licensing lets you gain driving skills and experience gradually, in lower-risk environments.
The two-step licensing system takes at least 20 months to complete and includes two road tests.
Passing the Level Two (G2) road test gives you full Class G driving privileges.
While the Level One road test deals with basic driving skills, the Level Two deals with advanced knowledge and skills that are generally gained with driving experience.
When you take the test, the examiner will give you directions.
As you complete the driving tasks, the examiner will watch to make sure you successfully perform the actions associated with them.
The G2 road test includes a component of expressway driving.

Off-road vehicles and snowmobiles are popular forms of recreation for many people in Ontario.
They are also necessary for transportation in remote areas and in emergencies.
But these vehicles are not toys.
If you intend to use them, you must know how they work, how to drive them safely in different situations and how Ontario laws apply to them.

vg: you must know how they work
label.v: an off-road vehicle driver MUST know how the vehicle works, how to drive it safely in different situations AND how ontario laws apply to it WHEN the driver intends to use an off-road vehicle OR snowmobile

text: It is important to remember that off-road vehicles are intended for off-road use.
Dirt bikes cannot be driven on public roads, although snowmobiles can be in some areas.

label.v: a dirt bike driver MUST NOT drive on public roads; a snowmobile driver MAY drive on public roads WHEN in an area where this is allowed

text: Off-road vehicles are allowed to travel directly across some highways.

label.v: an off-road vehicle driver MAY travel directly across a highway ONLY IF the highway is one where off-road vehicles are allowed to cross

text: However only single-rider, all-terrain vehicles can be driven on the shoulder of some provincial highways and municipal roads where bylaws permit.

vg: some provincial highways and municipal roads
only single-rider, all-terrain vehicles can be driven on the shoulder
label.v: an off-road vehicle driver MAY drive on the shoulder of a provincial highway OR municipal road ONLY IF the vehicle is a single-rider all-terrain vehicle AND bylaws permit it

text: This section of the handbook contains information about Ontario’s laws and safe driving tips for snowmobiles and off-road vehicles.
As you read, remember it is a guide only.

For official purposes, please refer to the Highway Traffic Act , the Motorized Snow Vehicles Act , the Off-road Vehicles Act , the Trespass to Property Act and the Occupiers' Liability Act of Ontario .
The applicable legislation can be accessed online through Ontario’s e-Laws website .
Note: Alcohol presents a major risk to your safety and the safety of others whether you are driving a car, motorcycle, snowmobile or off-road vehicle.
Drinking affects your ability to operate your vehicle and increases your chances of having a collision.
This chapter tells you what you need to know to drive a motorized snow vehicle in Ontario.
This includes age requirements, registration, where you can and cannot drive, safety tips, traffic signs and signals and the Snowmobiler’s Code of Ethics.

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Obey the speed limits
text: You must not drive a snowmobile faster than 20 km/h in any public park or exhibition ground, or on any road where the speed limit for other vehi­cles is 50 km/h or less.

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Obey the speed limits
text: You must not drive faster than 50 km/h on snowmobile trails or on any road where the speed limit for other vehicles is more than 50 km/h .

label.v: a snowmobile driver MUST NOT drive faster than 50 km/h WHEN the driver is on a snowmobile trail OR on a road where the speed limit for other vehicles is more than 50 km/h

text: Always leave extra space between you and the snowmobile in front to give yourself more time to react to unexpected hazards and stop safely.

text: Always wear clothing with reflective markings to remain visible at night.

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Obey the speed limits
text: Municipalities may set other speed limits for snowmobiles on public roads, trails and parks within their boundaries.

text: Check municipal bylaws.

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Stop for police
text: You must come to a safe stop when requested by a police officer to do so.

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Do not drink and drive
text: Alcohol is a major factor in snowmobile fatalities.

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Do not drink and drive
text: Consuming any amount of alcohol before you ride affects your ability to make good decisions.

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Do not drink and drive
text: Alcohol also increases fatigue, slows reaction time and increases your risk of hypothermia.

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Do not drink and drive
text: It is against the law to drive a snowmobile when you are impaired by alcohol or drugs.

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Do not drink and drive
text: Drinking and driving is a deadly combination.

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Do not drink and drive
text: All drivers, especially inexperienced drivers, must be able to concentrate on driving.

label.v: a driver MUST be able to concentrate on driving

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Do not drink and drive
text: Consuming any amount of alcohol before you ride affects your ability to make good decisions.

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Do not drink and drive
text: Even one drink can reduce your ability to concentrate and react to things that happen suddenly when you are driving.

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Do not drink and drive
text: With more alcohol in your blood, you could have trouble judging distances and your vision may become blurred.

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Do not drink and drive
text: Factors like tiredness, your mood, and how long ago you ate and how much, can make a difference in how alcohol affects your driving ability.

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Do not drink and drive
text: The police can stop any driver to determine if alcohol or drug testing is required.

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Do not drink and drive
text: They may also do roadside spot checks.

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Do not drink and drive
text: When stopped by the police, you may be told to blow into a machine that tests your breath for alcohol, a roadside screening device, or perform physical co-ordination tests.

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Do not drink and drive
text: If you fail or refuse to provide a breath sample or to perform the physical co-ordination tests, you will be charged under the Criminal Code.

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Do not drink and drive

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Do not drink and drive

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Do not drink and drive

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Do not drink and drive
text: If the police believe that a driver is impaired because of the consumption of a drug or a combination of alcohol and a drug, they can also require a driver to submit to an evaluation and then require a driver to provide blood, oral fluid or urine samples.

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Do not drink and drive

label.v: IF VIOLATED a charge under the Criminal Code WHEN the driver fails or refuses to comply with a police demand for an evaluation OR a blood, oral fluid or urine sample

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Do not drink and drive
text: Driving impaired or with more than 80 milligrams of alcohol in 100 millilitres of blood (.08) is an offence under the Criminal Code.

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Do not drink and drive
text: Even if your blood-alcohol concentration is less than .08, you can still be charged with impaired driving under the Criminal Code.

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Do not drink and drive
text: You will receive an immediate 90-day administrative driver’s licence suspension if your blood-alcohol concentration (BAC) is more than .08 or if you fail or refuse to provide a breath or bodily fluid sample, perform a physical co-ordination test or submit to an evaluation.

label.v: IF VIOLATED an immediate 90-day administrative licence suspension WHEN the driver's BAC is more than .08 OR the driver fails or refuses to provide a breath or bodily fluid sample, perform a physical co-ordination test OR submit to an evaluation

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Do not drink and drive
text: If you register in the “warn range” of .05 to .08 on a roadside screening device, you will receive an immediate driver’s licence suspension.

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Do not drink and drive

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Do not drink and drive

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Do not drink and drive
text: For a third or subsequent time in a five-year period, you will be immediately suspended for 30 days, and you must undergo a remedial alcohol-treatment program and have an ignition interlock condition placed on your licence for six months.

label.v: IF VIOLATED an immediate 30-day licence suspension AND a remedial alcohol-treatment program AND a six-month ignition interlock condition for a third or subsequent occurrence within a five-year period

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Do not drink and drive
text: If you choose not to install an ignition interlock device, you must not drive until the condition is removed from your licence.

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Do not drink and drive
text: If you are 21 years old and under and hold a full-class driver’s licence, you must not drive if you have been drinking alcohol.

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Do not drink and drive

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Do not drink and drive
text: Drivers of all ages in either Level One or Level Two of Ontario’s graduated licensing system must also have a blood-alcohol level of zero when driving.

label.v: a novice driver in Level One or Level Two MUST have a blood-alcohol level of zero WHEN driving

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Do not drink and drive
text: New drivers caught drinking and driving will receive an immediate driver’s licence suspension at the roadside for 24 hours and, if convicted, will face a fine and will receive a suspension period as per the Novice Driver Escalating Sanctions scheme.

label.v: IF VIOLATED an immediate 24-hour roadside licence suspension AND, on conviction, a fine AND a suspension under the Novice Driver Escalating Sanctions scheme

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Do not drink and drive
text: For the first occurrence, you will be suspended for 30 days.

label.v: IF VIOLATED a 30-day licence suspension for the first occurrence

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Do not drink and drive
text: For the second occurrence, in a five-year period, you will be suspended for 90 days.

label.v: IF VIOLATED a 90-day licence suspension for the second occurrence within a five-year period

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Do not drink and drive
text: For the third occurrence in a five-year period, the novice portion of your driver’s licence will be cancelled, and you must reapply for a G1 licence.

label.v: IF VIOLATED cancellation of the novice portion of the licence AND a requirement to reapply for a G1 licence for the third occurrence within a five-year period

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Do not drink and drive

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Drugs
text: You will also receive an immediate 90-day administrative driver’s licence suspension.

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Drugs
text: Illegal drugs such as marijuana and cocaine are not the only problem.

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Drugs
text: Some drugs that your doctor may prescribe for you and some over-the-counter drugs can also impair your driving.

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Drugs
text: Here are some points you should remember:

text: If you use prescription medicines or get allergy shots, ask your doctor about side effects such as dizziness, blurred vision, nausea or drowsiness that could affect your driving.

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Drugs
text: Read the information on the package of any over-the-counter medicine you take.

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Drugs
text: Any stimulant, diet pill, tranquillizer or sedative may affect your driving.

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Drugs
text: Even allergy and cold remedies may have ingredients that could affect your driving.

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Drugs
text: Drugs and any amount of alcohol together can have dangerous effects, even several days after you have taken the drug.

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Drugs
text: Do not take a chance - ask your doctor or pharmacist.

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Practice safe snowmobiling
text: Driving a snowmobile requires the same attention and alertness that driving any other kind of vehicle does.

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Practice safe snowmobiling

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Practice safe snowmobiling

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Practice safe snowmobiling

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Practice safe snowmobiling

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Practice safe snowmobiling

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Practice safe snowmobiling
text: Listen to local radio broadcast warnings by the Ontario Provincial Police about ice conditions.

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Practice safe snowmobiling

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Practice safe snowmobiling

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Practice safe snowmobiling

section: Driving a snowmobile > II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling > Practice safe snowmobiling
text: Carry a cell phone with you when riding.

section: Driving a snowmobile > III. Snowmobile signals and signs > Wind-chill factor
text: Wind-chill factor is the combined effect of wind and low temperature, which makes it feel much colder on a windy day in winter than is the actual temperature.

section: Driving a snowmobile > III. Snowmobile signals and signs > Wind-chill factor
text: This is caused by the faster cooling effect of the wind.

section: Driving a snowmobile > III. Snowmobile signals and signs > Wind-chill factor

section: Driving a snowmobile > III. Snowmobile signals and signs > Wind-chill factor

section: Driving a snowmobile > III. Snowmobile signals and signs > Wind-chill factor

Off-road vehicles (sometimes called ORVs) are any two- or three-wheeled motorized vehicles, as well as specific vehicles with four or more wheels as prescribed by regulation, intended for recreational use.

vg: specific vehicles with four or more wheels as prescribed by regulation
label.v: DEFINE off-road vehicle IS a motorized vehicle THAT has two or three wheels, OR has four or more wheels as prescribed by regulation, AND is intended for recreational use ALSO CALLED ORV

text: Examples of off-road vehicles include all-terrain vehicles (ATVs), two-up ATV s, side-by-side ATV s, utility terrain vehicles (UTVs), amphibious ATV s, off-road motorcycles and dune buggies.

label.v: DEFINE off-road vehicle IS a vehicle class THAT includes, for example, ATVs, two-up ATVs, side-by-side ATVs, UTVs, amphibious ATVs, off-road motorcycles AND dune buggies

text: Note: Electric and motorized scooters (commonly known as go-peds) and pocket bikes (which are miniature motorcycles about two feet in height and with a speed of 70-80 km/h ) are not off-road vehicles and, as such, cannot be registered as off-road vehicles.

label.v: DEFINE pocket bike IS a miniature motorcycle THAT is about two feet in height with a speed of 70-80 km/h; FACT electric and motorized scooters (ALSO CALLED go-peds) AND pocket bikes are NOT off-road vehicles AND cannot be registered as off-road vehicles

text: These vehicles also do not comply with motorcycle standards and cannot be registered as motorcycles.

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > I. Getting ready to drive an off-road vehicle > Make sure your vehicle is in good condition
text: Check that you have enough fuel and oil.

label.v: an off-road vehicle driver SHOULD check that there is enough fuel AND oil

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > I. Getting ready to drive an off-road vehicle > Make sure your vehicle is in good condition
text: Check that the engine is running smoothly.

label.v: an off-road vehicle driver SHOULD check that the engine is running smoothly

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > I. Getting ready to drive an off-road vehicle > Make sure your vehicle is in good condition
text: Make sure the is in neutral before starting the engine.

label.v: an off-road vehicle driver SHOULD make sure the transmission is in neutral WHEN the driver is about to start the engine

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > I. Getting ready to drive an off-road vehicle > Make sure your vehicle is in good condition
text: Check that your lights are in good working condition.

label.v: an off-road vehicle driver SHOULD check that the lights are in good working condition

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > I. Getting ready to drive an off-road vehicle > Make sure your vehicle is in good condition
text: Before you drive anywhere, read the owner’s manual.

label.v: an off-road vehicle driver SHOULD read the owner's manual WHEN the driver has not yet driven the vehicle anywhere

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > I. Getting ready to drive an off-road vehicle > Be well prepared for every trip
text: Carefully preparing for every trip is an important safety measure.

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > I. Getting ready to drive an off-road vehicle > Be well prepared for every trip
text: Check local weather forecasts and make sure you tell someone where you will be travelling and when you expect to be back.

label.v: an off-road vehicle driver SHOULD check local weather forecasts AND tell someone where the driver will be travelling AND when the driver expects to be back

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > I. Getting ready to drive an off-road vehicle > Be well prepared for every trip
text: Use the buddy system; drive with others, not alone.

label.v: an off-road vehicle driver SHOULD use the buddy system AND drive with others; an off-road vehicle driver SHOULD NOT drive alone

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > I. Getting ready to drive an off-road vehicle > Be well prepared for every trip
text: Take along a first-aid kit, a vehicle repair kit, an extra ignition key, a drive belt, spark plugs and a rope.

label.v: an off-road vehicle driver SHOULD take along a first-aid kit, a vehicle repair kit, an extra ignition key, a drive belt, spark plugs AND a rope WHEN the driver goes on a trip

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > I. Getting ready to drive an off-road vehicle > Be well prepared for every trip
text: On long trips, include a map and a compass (or a GPS unit and know how to use it), flashlight, hunting knife, hatchet, extra fuel and matches in a waterproof box.

label.v: an off-road vehicle driver SHOULD take along a map AND a compass (OR a GPS unit AND know how to use it), a flashlight, a hunting knife, a hatchet, extra fuel AND matches in a waterproof box WHEN the trip is long

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Where you can and cannot drive
text: You may not drive an off-road vehicle on most public roads in Ontario.

label.v: an off-road vehicle driver MUST NOT drive an off-road vehicle on most public roads in Ontario

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Where you can and cannot drive
text: This includes the area between the boundary or property lines, including medians, shoulders and ditches.

label.v: an off-road vehicle driver MUST NOT drive in the area between the boundary or property lines of such a road, including medians, shoulders AND ditches

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Where you can and cannot drive
text: There are some exceptions:

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Where you can and cannot drive
text: You may drive an off-road vehicle directly across some public roads.

label.v: an off-road vehicle driver MAY drive directly across some public roads (EXCEPTION TO an off-road vehicle driver MUST NOT drive on most public roads)

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Where you can and cannot drive
text: You may drive certain off-road vehicles with three or more wheels along some public roads when using the vehicle for farming, for licensed hunting or for the trapping of fur-bearing animals, provided that the vehicle weighs 450 kilograms or less and does not have an overall width greater than 1.35 metres (excluding mirrors).

label.v: an off-road vehicle driver MAY drive an off-road vehicle with three or more wheels along some public roads WHEN using it for farming, licensed hunting OR trapping fur-bearing animals ONLY IF the vehicle weighs 450 kg or less AND is no wider than 1.35 m excluding mirrors (EXCEPTION TO an off-road vehicle driver MUST NOT drive on most public roads)

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Where you can and cannot drive
text: You may drive an off-road vehicle within a provincial or public park if it is permitted by the park authority.

label.v: an off-road vehicle driver MAY drive within a provincial or public park ONLY IF the park authority permits it (EXCEPTION TO an off-road vehicle driver MUST NOT drive on most public roads)

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Where you can and cannot drive
text: Emergency personnel, such as police officers and firefighters, who are performing necessary duties in the course of their work or who are responding to an emergency, may drive off-road vehicles on public roads.

label.v: emergency personnel MAY drive off-road vehicles on public roads WHEN performing necessary duties in the course of their work OR responding to an emergency (EXCEPTION TO an off-road vehicle driver MUST NOT drive on most public roads)

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Where you can and cannot drive
text: There are also exceptions for the category of off-road vehicles known as all-terrain vehicles (ATVs).

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Where you can and cannot drive
text: If you do drive an off-road vehicle on or across a public road, you must be at least 16 years of age and have a valid Ontario driver’s licence (Class G2, M2 or higher).

label.v: an off-road vehicle driver MUST be at least 16 years of age AND have a valid Ontario driver's licence (Class G2, M2 or higher) WHEN the driver drives on or across a public road

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Where you can and cannot drive
text: You may not operate an ATV in such a way as to disrupt or destroy the natural environment, including fish habitats, property and plants or trees.

vg: in such a way as to disrupt
label.v: an ATV driver MUST NOT operate an ATV in a way that disrupts or destroys the natural environment, including fish habitats, property AND plants or trees

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Where you can and cannot drive
text: For more specific information on where you may operate off-road vehicles, and what rules you must follow when doing so, you should refer to the Highway Traffic Act and the Off-road Vehicles Act .

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > All-terrain vehicles (ATVs)
text: All-terrain vehicles are off-road vehicles with the following characteristics: four wheels, all of which are in contact with the ground; steering handlebars; and a seat designed to be straddled by the driver.

label.v: DEFINE all-terrain vehicle IS an off-road vehicle THAT has four wheels all in contact with the ground AND steering handlebars AND a seat designed to be straddled by the driver ALSO CALLED ATV

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > All-terrain vehicles (ATVs)
text: There are sections of provincial highways in Ontario where you may drive an ATV on the shoulder, provided the ATV weighs 450 kilograms or less, does not have an overall width greater than 1.35 metres (excluding mirrors), meets the requirements of the federal Motor Vehicle Safety Act and the American National Standards Institute Standard, and is designed to carry only a driver and no passengers.

vg: There are sections of provincial highways
label.v: an ATV driver MAY drive on the shoulder WHEN on a designated section of a provincial highway ONLY IF the ATV weighs 450 kg or less AND is no wider than 1.35 m excluding mirrors AND meets the federal Motor Vehicle Safety Act AND ANSI standard requirements AND is designed to carry only a driver and no passengers

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > All-terrain vehicles (ATVs)
text: You must travel in the same direction as the traffic using that side of the road.

label.v: an ATV driver MUST travel in the same direction as the traffic using that side of the road WHEN driving on the highway shoulder

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > All-terrain vehicles (ATVs)
text: If there is no shoulder, if the shoulder is obstructed or if you are crossing a level railway crossing, you may drive your vehicle on the paved part of the highway.

label.v: an ATV driver MAY drive on the paved part of the highway WHEN there is no shoulder OR the shoulder is obstructed OR the driver is crossing a level railway crossing (EXCEPTION TO an ATV driver MAY drive on the shoulder ONLY IF ...)

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > All-terrain vehicles (ATVs)
text: Keep as close as safely possible to the right of the shoulder or edge of the highway as you can.

vg: Keep as close as safely possible to the right
label.v: an ATV driver SHOULD keep as close as safely possible to the right edge of the shoulder or highway

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > All-terrain vehicles (ATVs)
text: Where a road or highway falls under the authority of a municipality, the municipality must enact a bylaw for ATV s to be allowed access to the road.

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > All-terrain vehicles (ATVs)
text: If there is no bylaw in place, you cannot drive an ATV on that road.

label.v: an ATV driver MUST NOT drive an ATV on a municipal road WHEN there is no bylaw in place allowing it

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > All-terrain vehicles (ATVs)
text: The municipality may also pass bylaws to decide where andwhen ATV s may be used on these local roads.

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > All-terrain vehicles (ATVs)
text: For those roads and highways where you are permitted to drive an ATV , you must obey all licensing and operational requirements, and your vehicle must conform to all equipment requirements, as listed in the Highway Traffic Act and the Off-road Vehicles Act .

label.v: an ATV driver MUST obey all licensing AND operational requirements AND the ATV MUST conform to all equipment requirements of the Highway Traffic Act AND the Off-road Vehicles Act WHEN the ATV is driven on a road or highway where ATVs are permitted

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > All-terrain vehicles (ATVs)
text: Remember the following rules:

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > All-terrain vehicles (ATVs)
text: You must have a valid Ontario driver’s licence (G2, M2 or higher).

label.v: an ATV driver MUST have a valid Ontario driver's licence (G2, M2 or higher) WHEN driving an ATV on a road or highway where ATVs are permitted

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > All-terrain vehicles (ATVs)
text: You must wear a motorcycle helmet with a chin strap that is securely fastened.

label.v: an ATV driver MUST wear a motorcycle helmet with a securely fastened chin strap WHEN driving an ATV on a road or highway where ATVs are permitted

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > All-terrain vehicles (ATVs)
text: You cannot carry passengers on your vehicle.

label.v: an ATV driver MUST NOT carry passengers WHEN driving an ATV on a road or highway where ATVs are permitted

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > All-terrain vehicles (ATVs)
text: You must drive at speed limits lower than those posted: where the posted speed is 50 km/h or less, you must drive 20 km/h or less; where the posted speed is over 50 km/h , you must drive 50 km/h or less.

label.v: an ATV driver MUST drive at 20 km/h or less WHEN the posted speed is 50 km/h or less; an ATV driver MUST drive at 50 km/h or less WHEN the posted speed is over 50 km/h

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > All-terrain vehicles (ATVs)
text: In general, ATV s are not permitted on controlled-access highways, such as the 400 series highways and most parts of the Trans-Canada Highway, but are allowed access to highways 500 to 899, the 7000 series highways and highways with low traffic volumes.

vg: most parts of the Trans-Canada Highway
label.v: an ATV driver MUST NOT drive on a controlled-access highway such as a 400 series highway OR most parts of the Trans-Canada Highway (in general); an ATV driver MAY drive on highways 500 to 899, the 7000 series highways AND highways with low traffic volumes

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > All-terrain vehicles (ATVs)
text: For more details about which highways ATV s may drive on, please refer to the Highway Traffic Act , Ontario Regulation 316/03.

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Obey the rules
text: You must stop if a police officer signals you to do so.

label.v: an off-road vehicle driver MUST stop WHEN a police officer signals the driver to do so

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Obey the rules
text: You can also be stopped by a landowner when you are driving on private property.

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Obey the rules
text: If signalled to stop by an authorized person, you must stop and, if asked, properly identify yourself.

label.v: an off-road vehicle driver MUST stop WHEN signalled to stop by an authorized person; the driver MUST properly identify themselves WHEN asked

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Obey the rules
text: Everyone who drives an off-road vehicle without care and attention or without reasonable consideration for other people and property may be charged with careless driving.

vg: without reasonable consideration for other people and property
label.v: IF VIOLATED a charge of careless driving WHEN an off-road vehicle driver drives without care and attention OR without reasonable consideration for other people and property

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Obey the rules
text: Other offences, such as dangerous driving and alcohol related offences, apply to drivers of off-road vehicles.

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Obey the rules
text: When you drive an off-road vehicle on a public road, the Highway Traffic Act offences also apply.

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Report collisions to the police
text: You must report to the police immediately any collision on a public highway that results in injury to any person or damage to property apparently exceeding $5,000.

label.v: an off-road vehicle driver MUST report the collision to the police immediately WHEN a collision on a public highway results in injury to any person OR damage to property apparently exceeding $5,000

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Do not drink and drive
text: It is against the law to drive an off-road vehicle when you are impaired by alcohol or drugs.

label.v: an off-road vehicle driver MUST NOT drive an off-road vehicle WHEN the driver is impaired by alcohol or drugs

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Do not drink and drive
text: Drinking and driving is a deadly combination.

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Do not drink and drive
text: Consuming any amount of alcohol before you ride affects your ability to make good decisions.

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Do not drink and drive
text: Even one drink can reduce your ability to concentrate and react to things that happen suddenly when you are driving.

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Do not drink and drive
text: With more alcohol in your blood, you could have trouble judging distances and your vision may become blurred.

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Do not drink and drive
text: Factors like tiredness, your mood, and how long ago you ate and how much, can make a difference in how alcohol affects your driving ability.

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Do not drink and drive
text: The police can stop any driver to determine if alcohol or drug testing is required.

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Do not drink and drive
text: They may also do roadside spot checks.

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Do not drink and drive
text: When stopped by the police, you may be told to blow into a machine that tests your breath for alcohol, a roadside screening device, or perform physical co-ordination tests.

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Do not drink and drive
text: If you fail or refuse to provide a breath sample or to perform the physical co-ordination tests, you will be charged under the Criminal Code.

vg: If you fail or refuse to provide a breath sample
label.v: IF VIOLATED a charge under the Criminal Code WHEN the driver fails or refuses to provide a breath sample OR to perform the physical co-ordination tests

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Do not drink and drive
text: If the reading on the machine shows you have been drinking, you may be taken to a police station for a breathalyzer test.

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Do not drink and drive
text: The breathalyzer uses your breath to measure the amount of alcohol in your bloodstream.

label.v: DEFINE breathalyzer IS a device THAT uses a person's breath to measure the amount of alcohol in the bloodstream

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Do not drink and drive
text: If you cannot give a breath sample or it is impractical to obtain a sample of breath, the police officer can require you to provide a blood sample instead.

vg: it is impractical to obtain a sample of breath

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Do not drink and drive
text: If the police believe that a driver is impaired because of the consumption of a drug or a combination of alcohol and a drug, they can also require a driver to submit to an evaluation and then require a driver to provide blood, oral fluid or urine samples.

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Do not drink and drive
text: If you fail or refuse to comply with any of these demands, you will be charged under the Criminal Code.

label.v: IF VIOLATED a charge under the Criminal Code WHEN the driver fails or refuses to comply with a police demand for an evaluation OR a blood, oral fluid or urine sample

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Do not drink and drive
text: Driving impaired or with more than 80 milligrams of alcohol in 100 millilitres of blood (.08) is an offence under the Criminal Code.

label.v: a driver MUST NOT drive WHEN the driver is impaired OR has more than 80 milligrams of alcohol in 100 millilitres of blood

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Do not drink and drive
text: Even if your blood-alcohol concentration (BAC) is less than .08, you can still be charged with impaired driving under the Criminal Code.

label.v: IF VIOLATED a charge of impaired driving under the Criminal Code WHEN the driver is impaired even though the blood-alcohol concentration is less than .08

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Do not drink and drive
text: You will receive an immediate 90-day administrative driver’s licence suspension if BAC is more than .08 or if you fail or refuse to provide a breath or bodily fluid sample, perform a physical co-ordination test or submit to an evaluation.

label.v: IF VIOLATED an immediate 90-day administrative licence suspension WHEN the driver's BAC is more than .08 OR the driver fails or refuses to provide a breath or bodily fluid sample, perform a physical co-ordination test OR submit to an evaluation

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Do not drink and drive
text: If you register in the “warn range” of .05 to .08 on a roadside screening device, you will receive an immediate driver’s licence suspension.

label.v: IF VIOLATED an immediate licence suspension WHEN the driver registers in the warn range of .05 to .08 on a roadside screening device

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Do not drink and drive
text: For a first occurrence, you will be suspended for three days.

label.v: IF VIOLATED a three-day licence suspension for a first occurrence

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Do not drink and drive
text: For a second occurrence in a five-year period, you will be immediately suspended for seven days and you must undergo a remedial alcohol-education program.

label.v: IF VIOLATED an immediate seven-day licence suspension AND a remedial alcohol-education program for a second occurrence within a five-year period

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Do not drink and drive
text: For a third or subsequent time in a five-year period, you will be immediately suspended for 30 days, and you must undergo a remedial alcohol-treatment program and have an ignition interlock condition placed on your licence for six months.

label.v: IF VIOLATED an immediate 30-day licence suspension AND a remedial alcohol-treatment program AND a six-month ignition interlock condition for a third or subsequent occurrence within a five-year period

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Do not drink and drive
text: If you choose not to install an ignition interlock device, you must not drive until the condition is removed from your licence.

label.v: a driver MUST NOT drive WHEN the driver has an ignition interlock condition AND has not installed an ignition interlock device (... UNTIL the condition is removed from the licence)

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Do not drink and drive
text: If you are 21 years old and under and hold a full-class driver’s licence, you must not drive if you have been drinking alcohol.

label.v: a driver aged 21 or under who holds a full-class licence MUST NOT drive WHEN the driver has been drinking alcohol

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Do not drink and drive
text: Your blood-alcohol level must be zero.

label.v: a driver aged 21 or under MUST have a blood-alcohol level of zero WHILE driving

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Do not drink and drive
text: If you are caught driving with alcohol in your blood, you will receive an immediate driver’s licence suspension at the roadside for 24 hours and, if convicted, you will face a fine and a 30-day licence suspension.

label.v: IF VIOLATED an immediate 24-hour roadside licence suspension AND, on conviction, a fine AND a 30-day licence suspension

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Do not drink and drive
text: Drivers of all ages in either Level One or Level Two of Ontario’s graduated licensing system must also have a blood-alcohol level of zero when driving.

label.v: a novice driver in Level One or Level Two MUST have a blood-alcohol level of zero WHEN driving

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Do not drink and drive
text: New drivers caught drinking and driving will receive an immediate driver’s licence suspension at the roadside for 24 hours and, if convicted, will face a fine and will receive a suspension period as per the Novice Driver Escalating Sanctions scheme.

label.v: IF VIOLATED an immediate 24-hour roadside licence suspension AND, on conviction, a fine AND a suspension under the Novice Driver Escalating Sanctions scheme

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Do not drink and drive
text: For the first occurrence, you will be suspended for 30 days.

label.v: IF VIOLATED a 30-day licence suspension for the first occurrence

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Do not drink and drive
text: For the second occurrence, in a five-year period, you be suspended for 90 days.

label.v: IF VIOLATED a 90-day licence suspension for the second occurrence within a five-year period

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Do not drink and drive
text: For the third occurrence in a five-year period, the novice portion of your driver’s licence will be cancelled, and you must reapply for a G1 licence.

label.v: IF VIOLATED cancellation of the novice portion of the licence AND a requirement to reapply for a G1 licence for the third occurrence within a five-year period

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Do not drink and drive
text: Novice drivers will also be charged under the Criminal Code if their BAC exceeds .08 and will be issued a “warn range” suspension if they register a BAC from .05 to .08.

label.v: IF VIOLATED a charge under the Criminal Code WHEN the novice driver's BAC exceeds .08; IF VIOLATED a warn-range suspension WHEN the novice driver registers a BAC from .05 to .08

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Drugs
text: Any drug that changes your mood or the way you see and feel about the world around you will affect the way you drive.

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Drugs
text: Criminal Code and HTA sanctions apply to drivers impaired by alcohol or a drug.

label.v: IF VIOLATED Criminal Code AND HTA sanctions WHEN the driver is impaired by alcohol or a drug

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Drugs
text: In circumstances involving possible impairment by a drug or a combination of alcohol and a drug, police can require a driver to perform physical co-ordination tests and to submit to an evaluation and then require a driver to provide blood, oral fluid or urine samples.

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Drugs
text: If you fail or refuse to comply with any of these demands, you will be charged under the Criminal Code.

label.v: IF VIOLATED a charge under the Criminal Code WHEN the driver fails or refuses to comply with a police demand for co-ordination tests, an evaluation OR a blood, oral fluid or urine sample

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Drugs
text: You will also receive an immediate 90-day administrative driver’s licence suspension.

label.v: IF VIOLATED an immediate 90-day administrative licence suspension

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Drugs
text: Illegal drugs such as marijuana and cocaine are not the only problem.

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Drugs
text: Some drugs that your doctor may prescribe for you and some over-the-counter drugs can also impair your driving.

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Drugs
text: Here are some points you should remember:

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Drugs
text: If you use prescription medicines or get allergy shots, ask your doctor about side effects such as dizziness, blurred vision, nausea or drowsiness that could affect your driving.

label.v: a driver SHOULD ask a doctor about side effects that could affect driving, such as dizziness, blurred vision, nausea or drowsiness, WHEN the driver uses prescription medicines OR gets allergy shots

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Drugs
text: Read the information on the package of any over-the-counter medicine you take.

label.v: a driver SHOULD read the information on the package WHEN the driver takes an over-the-counter medicine

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Drugs
text: Any stimulant, diet pill, tranquillizer or sedative may affect your driving.

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Drugs
text: Even allergy and cold remedies may have ingredients that could affect your driving.

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Drugs
text: Drugs and any amount of alcohol together can have dangerous effects, even several days after you have taken the drug.

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Drugs
text: Do not take a chance; ask your doctor or pharmacist.

label.v: a driver SHOULD ask a doctor or pharmacist about the effects of a drug on driving

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Do not carry passengers
text: Do not carry passengers on an off-road vehicle designed for one person.

vg: Do not carry passengers on an off-road vehicle designed for one person.
label.v: an off-road vehicle driver SHOULD NOT carry passengers WHEN the off-road vehicle is designed for one person

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Do not carry passengers
text: Carrying passengers changes the weight distribution of the vehicle and limits your ability to shift position on the vehicle for control and stability.

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Practice safe driving skills
text: Driving an off-road vehicle is different than driving any other type of vehicle, and takes more skill than you might think.

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Practice safe driving skills
text: Be sure to read your owner’s manual before you begin to drive.

label.v: an off-road vehicle driver SHOULD read the owner's manual WHEN the driver is about to begin driving

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Practice safe driving skills
text: If you are a beginner, practise driving your vehicle in an open area that is free of obstacles, until you become skilled at handling it.

label.v: an off-road vehicle driver SHOULD practise driving in an open area free of obstacles WHEN the driver is a beginner (... UNTIL the driver becomes skilled at handling the vehicle)

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Practice safe driving skills
text: Choose ground that is uniform, either dirt, sand or snow.

label.v: an off-road vehicle driver SHOULD choose uniform ground of dirt, sand OR snow WHEN practising as a beginner

section: Driving an Off-road vehicle > II. Safe and responsible off-road vehicle driving > Practice safe driving skills
text: Avoid paved surfaces when driving an off-road vehicle.

label.v: an off-road vehicle driver SHOULD NOT drive on paved surfaces WHEN driving an off-road vehicle
